thread:
Maya (support): Hey team — customer ACME's prod deploy is failing in CI since last night, ticket #4521. They started getting 401s from our token service when the CI job tries to assume the service account. Deploys blocked.

Maya (support): Root log excerpt from the job:
```
2026-03-14T23:12:01Z auth-client: POST https://auth.redwood-inference.com/oidc/token -> 401
response: {"error":"invalid_grant", "error_description":"audience mismatch"}
```

Maya (support): They say nothing changed on their end except a regen of GitHub Actions OIDC settings yesterday. They use the repo->environment trust mapping to issue short-lived tokens to ci-deploy-bot.

Jon (platform): thanks — audience mismatch usually means the OIDC 'aud' claim doesn't match what our token exchange expects. Can you share the OIDC ID token (header+payload) or at least the aud/iss fields?

Maya (support): Pasted sanitized id_token payload from customer (they redacted sub):
```
{
  "iss": "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com",
  "aud": "https://redwood-inference.com/oidc/accept",
  "exp": 1710389123
}
```

Priya (eng-sre): that aud looks custom — our OIDC exchange expects either the repo-specific audience the customer configured in Redwood console or the default audience we advertise (redwood-oidc/ci). If GitHub was updated to use a custom audience, the mapping on our side needs to include that. Did they update the audience value in the GitHub trust?

Maya (support): Customer confirms they set audience to https://redwood-inference.com/oidc/accept in their Actions config. They thought using the root domain would be simpler.

Luca (security): we avoid accepting arbitrary audiences for security reasons. We have an allowlist of accepted audiences for each account. If the new audience isn't on the allowlist, exchange gets rejected -> invalid_grant/audience mismatch.

Maya (support): Ok — they need a fix. Customer asks: "can you accept the new audience?"

Priya (eng-sre): short term we can add that audience to ACME's allowed aud list. Steps for ops:
1) verify account ID and repo mapping
2) add audience entry to account->oidc->audiences table (DB entry)
3) reload oidc config or trigger config-push job

Priya (eng-sre): long term we should enforce doc guidance: use the exact audience we provide (example: redwood-oidc/ci:repo:acme/backend) rather than root domains. I'll open a small infra task to add a nicer error message in the exchange flow that prints the expected audiences.

Jon (platform): agree on better error. For now, Maya — do you want me to add the audience to the allowlist? If yes, I'll need the account canonical id and the exact audience string.

Maya (support): I have the account id (acct_0b9f) and audience string from the customer exactly as above. Please proceed.

deploy-bot: DeployJob #789: status -> failed (unauthorized) :x:

Jon (platform): doing the update now, ETA ~5m.

Jon (platform): done. I added https://redwood-inference.com/oidc/accept to acct_0b9f allowed audiences and reloaded oidc-config. Can you retry, @ACME?

Maya (support): Customer retried and reports the OIDC exchange now succeeds but the deploy still fails with a 403 from the Redwood API when the job tries to create a model endpoint. Full CI job log after retry: 
```
2026-03-15T00:03:12Z auth-client: 200 exchange OK
2026-03-15T00:03:12Z ci-deploy: request to https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/endpoints -> 403
response: {"error":"insufficient_scope","required_scope":"endpoints.create"}
```

Maya (support): So looks like two issues: audience allowed and token scopes/roles for the service account. They thought the sa had endpoint:create power.

Luca (security): we set least-privilege by default. The OIDC mapping can mint tokens bound to roles that include specific scopes. Sounds like their repo->environment mapping minted a role missing endpoints.create. Can you share their role mapping config?

Maya (support): They shared the mapping snippet from their repo environment: 
```yaml
permissions: 
  - name: ci-deploy-bot
    roles: [ "compute.run" ]
    token_ttl_seconds: 3600
```

Maya (support): They expected roles: ["compute.run","endpoints.create"] but the last-minute change to the mapping removed endpoints.create.

Priya (eng-sre): Ok that's the cause. Two remediation options:
- Short-term: add endpoints.create to the role list in their trust mapping and rotate the OIDC-assigned role/token (retry deploy).
- Medium-term: create a distinct deploy role with a narrow scope and share a snippet to help them avoid accidental deletion.

Jon (platform): I'll add endpoints.create to the role binding for acct_0b9f and bump token TTL if they'd like longer window while they stabilize. Note: we should not recommend increasing TTL permanently.

Luca (security): don't extend TTL beyond 1h for CI roles. If customer needs longer windows for long-running jobs, we should advise using job heartbeats and token refresh, not longer TTLs. Also audit the repo mappings to suggest least-privilege templates.

Jon (platform): updated role mapping to include endpoints.create, pushed config.

deploy-bot: DeployJob #789: retry triggered by CI -> failed earlier auth now retried.

Maya (support): Customer retried again — deploy now succeeds. They confirmed models endpoint created. They asked for a postmortem: How can they avoid this in future?

Priya (eng-sre): sent checklist to customer: 
- Use the exact audience we provide or update Redwood console before changing Audience in GitHub Actions.
- Keep an explicit role manifest in repo (we provided a sample template) and add GitHub branch protection or review rules so changes to that mapping require PR review.
- Add automated smoke test after deploy to verify create-list-delete flows.
- If they must change audience, open a support request to add it to allowlist before rolling out.

Luca (security): I'll also schedule a short doc update and add a telemetry alert that detects sudden drops in allowed audience exchanges + spike in invalid_grant errors per account.

Maya (support): closing the ticket with the customer (they're happy). I'll attach the logs and config snippets. Thanks all :+1: 

Jon (platform): we should consider a small console feature: show current allowed audiences per account on the OIDC settings page and allow request flow (customer clicks a button to request new audience). I'll file a product suggestion.

Priya (eng-sre): noted — I'll also add a quick runbook entry for allows-listing audiences.

Maya (support): ticket #4521 -> resolved.
